1996-08-23: Osama bin Laden issued a Declaration of War fatwa from his hideout in Afghanistan, calling for attacks on Americans and the overthrow of the Saudi government.
1998-12-24: Osama bin Laden held a press conference in Kandahar, Afghanistan, where he denied masterminding the US embassy bombings in Africa but said he supported the attacks and knew some of those involved.
1999-01-29: Three suspected Muslim extremists linked to Osama bin Laden were arrested in Uruguay with false passports while en route to London.
1999-02-10: The Taliban orchestrated Osama bin Laden's disappearance, spiriting him to an abandoned mountain guerrilla base and assigning 10 armed men to protect and guide him.
1999-02-13: Taliban authorities said Osama bin Laden was missing and that they did not know where he had gone.
1999-02-25: A newspaper report cites senior US intelligence officials saying Osama bin Laden attempted at least seven vehicle-bomb attacks on US embassies and military installations since the August 1998 east African embassy bombings, with the attacks prevented after US intelligence satellites intercepted his telephone calls from Afghanistan.
1999-05-19: A former US Army sergeant, Ali Mohamed, was indicted on charges of conspiring with Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida to kill Americans abroad, including the 1998 US embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania.
1999-07-11: Two Egyptians were arrested in London and accused of conspiring with Osama bin Laden to murder US citizens in the 1998 embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania.
1999-11-12: Osama bin Laden came under immediate suspicion after a series of rocket attacks on American and United Nations targets in Islamabad.
1999-12-19: US security experts intensified efforts to determine whether an arrested Algerian was part of a wider bombing network possibly involving Osama bin Laden, amid heightened millennium attack fears.
2000-05-17: President Bill Clinton accused the terrorist organisation allegedly operated by Osama bin Laden of plotting to harm Americans gathered for millennium celebrations.
2000-07-27: Taliban leader Mullah Omar refuses to hand over Osama bin Laden to the US, saying extradition would be tantamount to leaving a pillar of Islam, and suggests trial in an Islamic court if sufficient evidence exists.
2000-10-18: A leading US terrorism expert suggests the USS Cole bombing may have been the first joint operation between Osama bin Laden and Saddam Hussein.
2000-11-30: The high court ruled that Khalid al Fawwaz, a Saudi dissident allegedly linked to Osama bin Laden, should be extradited to the US to face charges of conspiracy to murder.
2001-01-03: Four men appeared in a US court in a trial in which prosecutors seek to try Osama bin Laden in absentia for the 1998 bombings of two US embassies that killed 224 people.
2001-02-05: Osama bin Laden is named as the central figure in the US trial of four men accused of conspiring with him to bomb two US embassies in Africa in 1998, though he remains at large and is believed to be in Afghanistan.
2001-02-06: A secret witness testified in a Manhattan federal court about his dealings with Osama bin Laden in the trial of four men accused of bombing two American embassies in 1998.
2001-03-03: A secretly taped conversation between Islamist extremists indicates that an attack by Osama bin Laden's guerrillas in Britain was foiled as they were on the point of striking, according to an Italian police report.
2001-03-30: Taliban supreme leader Mullah Mohammed Omar privately ruled out handing over Osama bin Laden for trial, saying he is ready to sacrifice what is left of Afghanistan before giving up his guest to the US.
2001-05-29: A New York jury convicts four members of an Islamic militant group led by Osama bin Laden for the 1998 US embassy bombings in east Africa, marking the first US conviction of anyone charged with crimes stemming from bin Laden's activities.
2001-09-05: Arab fighters funded by Osama bin Laden have become increasingly influential within Afghanistan's Taliban movement and are building a foreign legion to extend the regime's hardline vision of Islam, according to aid workers and analysts.
2001-09-11: American officials briefed journalists that Osama bin Laden is their number one suspect in the attacks.
US and Western intelligence organizations place Osama bin Laden at the top of the list of suspects within hours of the attacks in New York and Washington, though he denies responsibility.

An Arab journalist said Osama bin Laden had warned three weeks earlier that his group would carry out an unprecedented attack on US interests, and that Islamic fundamentalists led by Bin Laden were “almost certainly” behind the World Trade Centre attack, while a Taliban spokesman denied Bin Laden could be responsible.
Residents in Jeddah dismiss reports that Osama bin Laden telephoned his mother before the September 11 attacks to say he could not visit because something big was about to happen.

A gruesome video showing Islamic extremists murdering and mutilating 'infidels' was smuggled into the UK only days before the 11 September attacks, produced by the Salafist Group for Preaching and War (GSPC), an extremist Algerian organisation backed by Osama bin Laden.

Security chiefs on both sides of the Atlantic repeatedly turned down the chance to acquire a vast intelligence database on Osama bin Laden and more than 200 leading members of his al-Qaeda terrorist network in the years leading up to the 11 September attacks.
Hijackers fly planes into the World Trade Center and Pentagon, and Washington blames Osama bin Laden and tells the Taliban to hand him over.
Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida were responsible for the September 11 suicide hijackings, which were only a fraction of the hundreds of attacks they had planned.
The attacks on the US culminate a large network of Osama bin Laden supporters' schemes to kill westerners.
Taliban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar's refusal to hand over Osama bin Laden after the September 11 attacks infuriated his lieutenants.
2001-09-13: Osama bin Laden is officially declared the prime suspect behind the New York and Washington terrorist attacks, as a Congressional report reveals his al-Qaida network is identified or suspected in 34 countries.
2001-09-14: Western intelligence sources focus on the theory that Saudi-born terrorist Osama bin Laden was responsible for the September 11 attacks on New York City and Washington.
FBI released names of 19 hijackers and intelligence sources said information confirmed their suspected link to Osama bin Laden.
2001-09-17: Taliban supreme leader Mullah Mohammed Omar lets a grand council of Islamic clerics decide whether to hand over Osama bin Laden to the United States.
The US gives the Taliban a final three-day ultimatum, delivered via a Pakistani delegation, to hand over Osama bin Laden or face military attack.
2001-09-18: The Taliban’s most senior body of clerics is poised to declare a holy war against the US if a last-minute plea from Pakistan fails to persuade them to hand over Osama bin Laden.
2001-09-19: The Taliban's ruling Islamic council is expected to make a final decision on Osama bin Laden's fate, as it considers a last-minute deal to hand him over and avoid US retribution.
2001-09-20: The Taliban’s Islamic council proposed that Osama bin Laden be asked to leave Afghanistan voluntarily, but the US rejected the proposal as insufficient.
2001-09-22: Four people arrested in connection with the World Trade Center attacks continued to be held amid heightened fears of a British al-Qaeda cell linked to Osama bin Laden.
2001-09-23: A fax signed by Osama bin Laden called on "our beloved brothers" to "triumph over the infidel forces and the forces of tyranny, and to destroy the new Jewish-Christian crusader campaign on the soil of Pakistan and Afghanistan," though it may never be known if the fax came from his pen.
Saudi Arabia rejects a US request to use its air bases for an offensive against Osama bin Laden.
2001-09-24: President George W. Bush announces a freeze on US assets of Osama bin Laden and 26 other individuals and organizations in an effort to cut off terrorist funding.
Osama bin Laden issued a call to Muslims to join a holy war against infidel forces and pledged to fight alongside his Taliban hosts against any American invasion.
2001-09-25: Saudi Arabia cut all ties with the Taliban regime, accusing it of recruiting and training Saudis for international terrorism and marking its first public admission of citizens' links to Afghanistan and Osama bin Laden.

Journalist Hans Lindquist recalls meeting Osama bin Laden and his brother Salem in Falun, Sweden, in the early 1970s, after photos from his story resurfaced in UK newspapers following the September 11 attacks.
Lawyers for the Muwafaq Foundation deny that the charity supports Osama bin Laden and say their clients condemn the New York attacks.
2001-09-27: The Taliban confirms that Osama bin Laden is still in Afghanistan and states a messenger was dispatched to deliver an edict asking him to leave the country.
Iraq denies having any contact with Osama bin Laden or Afghanistan's Taliban government, and denies reports of a 1998 meeting between Bin Laden and Iraqi intelligence officials.
2001-09-28: A delegation of senior Islamic clerics told Taliban leader Mullah Mohammed Omar that handing over Osama bin Laden was the only way to avoid a US assault, while bin Laden reportedly denied involvement in the September 11 attacks.
A delegation of high-ranking Pakistani religious leaders and government officials arrives in Afghanistan for talks with the Taliban on the fate of Osama bin Laden.
2001-09-30: The Taliban admits that Osama bin Laden is being hidden at a secret location inside Afghanistan for his safety and security.
2001-10-03: The US handed Pakistan evidence of Osama bin Laden's involvement in the September 11 attacks, aiming to shore up support for a potential military assault on Afghanistan.
2001-10-04: Tony Blair released a dossier of evidence linking Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida to the September 11 attacks.

Pakistan said it believed there was conclusive evidence linking Osama bin Laden to the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Centre and the Pentagon, calling the US dossier a sufficient basis for indictment.

The CIA reportedly trained and armed around 60 Pakistani commandos in 1999 for a secret plan to kill or capture Osama bin Laden, an operation abandoned later that year after General Pervez Musharraf ousted Nawaz Sharif.
2001-10-05: The US and Britain are working on a diplomatic plan to topple the Taliban, preferably before any military strike against Osama bin Laden, the main suspect for the New York and Washington attacks.

US and allied intelligence officials were analyzing newly released, undated video footage of Osama bin Laden and his followers to determine whether it might represent a claim of responsibility for the September 11 attacks, a warning of more terrorism to come, or both.
2001-10-06: US investigators identify Saudi hijacker Khalid al-Mihdhar as a key link connecting Osama bin Laden to the Pentagon attack and the USS Cole and East Africa embassy bombings.
2001-10-07: The US and Britain launched a massive air campaign against Afghanistan targeting Osama bin Laden, his al-Qaida organization, and the ruling Taliban.
Osama bin Laden issued a pre-recorded video statement to al-Jazeera calling on Muslims to rise up against "infidels" immediately after Sunday night's attacks on Afghanistan.
2001-10-08: Demonstrators held up a poster of terror suspect Osama bin Laden during a pro-bin Laden rally in Bangladesh.
2001-10-10: The US government believes Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida may be sending coded messages via recent videos aired on al-Jazeera, possibly signaling a second wave of attacks.
2001-10-11: US government planners are looking at links between Osama bin Laden's al-Qaida network and Islamist groups in south-east Asia, particularly Indonesia, the Philippines and Malaysia.
2001-10-12: Osama bin Laden's son Abdullah claims his father is hiding in Afghanistan's mountains with 300 commandos and will never be captured by the West.

Intelligence presented to President Bush indicates Osama bin Laden provided an estimated $100 million in cash and military assistance to the Taliban over five years, leading the CIA to conclude he "owns and operates" the Taliban.
The Bush administration and British government froze the assets of 39 additional individuals and organizations, including Osama bin Laden and the al-Qaida network.
2001-10-14: The Taliban offers to discuss handing over Osama bin Laden to a neutral third country if the US halts its bombing of Afghanistan, but President Bush rejects the offer as "non-negotiable."
2001-10-15: Yassin al-Qadi, named by the US and UK as a terrorist supporter, denies allegations that his Jersey-based Muwafaq Foundation was a front for funding Osama bin Laden's al-Qaida.
2001-10-16: A senior Taliban minister offered a last-minute deal to hand over Osama bin Laden for trial in a third country without first seeing evidence, in exchange for a halt to bombing, during a secret visit to Islamabad.
A man claiming to represent al-Qaida asked CNN and al-Jazeera to submit written questions to be answered on video by Osama bin Laden.
2001-10-17: Letters allegedly written by Osama bin Laden to supporters in London were published, calling on al-Qaida members to acquire weapons of mass destruction and to "kill, fight, create traps and destroy" Americans, though a lawyer for one suspect expressed strong scepticism about their authenticity.
2001-10-18: Osama bin Laden's son Abdullah bin Laden denies that an interview published in the Sunday Mirror was with him, calling it completely fabricated.
Three Osama bin Laden followers convicted in the 1998 US embassy bombings in Africa were sentenced to life without parole in New York.
2001-10-20: Al-Jazeera obtained an exclusive interview with Osama bin Laden in Afghanistan that it never broadcast.
2001-10-21: An alleged al-Qaida member wanted in connection with the 1998 US embassy bombings in Africa claims he was in frequent contact with British security services, including MI5, and that this will show the limited extent of his involvement with Osama bin Laden's organization.
2001-10-22: The US government alleges that London-based Saudi businessman Khalid Al-Fawwaz finalised and edited Osama bin Laden's declaration of jihad against the US and acted as a key aide in a conspiracy to murder Americans, as Al-Fawwaz appeals against extradition to America.
2001-10-24: Tony Blair said the war would continue until Osama bin Laden was given up or killed, as US bombing continued in Afghanistan.
2001-11-05: Former Saudi intelligence chief Prince Turki al-Faisal says Taliban leader Mullah Mohammed Omar agreed in 1998 to hand over Osama bin Laden but reversed the decision after US cruise missile attacks.
2001-11-07: Al-Jazeera TV broadcasts unverifiable and undated footage said to show four of Osama bin Laden's sons holding weapons, reciting poetry, and looking at wreckage inside Afghanistan.
President George W. Bush widens the battle against Osama bin Laden by targeting Islamic money exchanges in the US and seeking to freeze assets in nine countries.
2001-11-08: Osama bin Laden gave a two-hour interview to Pakistani journalist Hamid Mir near Kabul, in which he stated Muslims have the right to attack America in reprisal and claimed to possess chemical and nuclear weapons as a deterrent.
2001-11-14: The Taliban states that Osama bin Laden and Mullah Mohammad Omar are safe in Afghanistan and that there is no change in their position on handing him over.
Tony Blair confirms several thousand British troops are on alert for Afghanistan duty and states the mission will not be finished until Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida are captured or suppressed.
2001-11-15: Mohammed Atef, a former military commander of al-Qaida and relative by marriage to Osama bin Laden, was killed in a US missile strike by coalition forces south of Kabul.
2001-11-17: A Taliban envoy claims Osama bin Laden has left Afghanistan with his children and wives, while a US intelligence official says there is no evidence he has left.
Documents found in Kabul link Osama bin Laden's al-Qaeda network and the Taliban to the September 11 attacks, including a flight simulator program and a list of US flight schools.
2001-11-18: Documents found in Kabul after the Taliban’s fall reveal al-Qaeda’s plans to send members to the United States to learn how to pilot passenger jets and indicate Taliban support for such plans.
2001-11-20: More than 2,000 US marines are on standby in the Arabian Sea and Pakistan for a potential manhunt for Osama bin Laden.
2001-11-21: The US is sending a Global Hawk reconnaissance drone to Afghanistan to track Osama bin Laden, as allies intensify the hunt for him and his al-Qaida network.
2001-11-22: British troops joined the hunt for Osama bin Laden and Taliban and al-Qaida fighters, as confirmed by Foreign Secretary Jack Straw.
2001-11-25: The United States is poised to dispatch about 2,000 elite Marines, supplemented by Navy Seals and Delta Force, into Afghanistan with orders to shoot Osama bin Laden on sight.
2001-12-03: A close aide claims Osama bin Laden fled Afghanistan to Pakistan about 10 days earlier with the help of local tribesmen, a claim greeted with scepticism by the US State Department.
2001-12-06: Osama bin Laden was reportedly seen in Tora Bora at the end of the previous week, though it was unclear whether he remained in the cave complex as Afghan mojahedin forces, backed by US bombing, seized parts of the al-Qaida base.
2001-12-07: Afghan fighters claim Osama bin Laden was seen on horseback with guards near the Tora Bora caves, though the sighting is unconfirmed.
2001-12-08: Osama bin Laden was sighted around the Tora Bora massif, where his al-Qaeda fighters, including dozens of British Muslims, were fighting a last-ditch battle in a cave complex near Jalalabad.
2001-12-09: US B-52s began carpet-bombing al-Qaida caves at Tora Bora in an increasingly difficult battle against Arab forces loyal to Osama bin Laden, who is thought to be leading the defence of Tora Bora with about 1,000 Arab fighters.
Britain’s defence secretary said Britain would hand over Osama bin Laden to the US only if he would not face the death penalty.
2001-12-11: Osama bin Laden's al-Qaida fighters were driven from their last stronghold in Tora Bora, Afghanistan, though bin Laden's whereabouts remained unknown.
2001-12-13: The Pentagon releases a captured videotape in which Osama bin Laden describes planning the September 11 attacks and says the hijackers were not told the full mission until just before boarding the planes.
2001-12-14: US defence sources say Osama bin Laden is most likely trapped in the Tora Bora region of eastern Afghanistan, though officials stress they are not sure of his location.
2001-12-15: A notebook found in an al-Qaeda camp in Kandahar reveals a detailed plan to bomb Moorgate in the City of London, indicating Osama bin Laden’s network was orchestrating a global terrorism campaign against Western interests.
2001-12-17: The House of Lords dismissed appeals by three men alleged to have conspired with Osama bin Laden to bomb US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania, clearing the way for their extradition to the US.

Speculation mounts over Osama bin Laden's whereabouts as anti-Taliban commanders believe he escaped Tora Bora up to a week earlier, while unconfirmed reports claim he slipped past Pakistani border patrols.
2001-12-18: The hunt for Osama bin Laden and the destruction of his al-Qaida forces continued as two US warplanes came under missile fire in Afghanistan, with no sign of Bin Laden found.
2001-12-26: A frozen corpse found by Pakistani villagers near the Afghan border may have been a French member of Osama bin Laden's al-Qaida network.
Al-Jazeera broadcasts excerpts of a new video-tape of Osama bin Laden, suggesting he was still alive as recently as about two weeks earlier.
2001-12-27: Afghanistan's defence ministry claims Osama bin Laden escaped across the border into Pakistan and is being sheltered by the extremist Pakistani movement Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, a claim rejected by the group and doubted by Pakistani officials.
2002-01-08: The US military is winding up its search for Osama bin Laden in the Tora Bora cave complex in eastern Afghanistan after failing to find him there.
2002-01-11: A federal judge in Manhattan rules that two families bereaved by the September 11 attacks can notify Osama bin Laden of their lawsuit by screening TV advertisements on al-Jazeera, since he cannot be served in person.
2002-01-20: US investigators are actively searching for Abu Zubeida, who is seen as the most likely successor to Osama bin Laden as head of al-Qaeda if bin Laden and Ayman al-Zawahiri are killed or captured.
2002-02-01: CNN broadcasts a previously unaired October 2001 interview in which Osama bin Laden justifies the September 11 attacks and warns the West, after al-Jazeera allegedly suppressed the footage.
2002-02-24: A senior al-Qaeda leader arrested in France told interrogators he saw hundreds of British recruits during four years as a trainer in Osama bin Laden's camps in eastern Afghanistan.
2002-03-20: US officials say a GPS device found in an Afghan cave might tie Osama bin Laden's al-Qaida network to the 1993 Somalia firefight that killed 18 American special forces troops, though a Pentagon spokesman says it might instead have reached Afghanistan through a black market transaction.
2002-03-27: A London-based Arabic newspaper says it received an email purporting to be from Osama bin Laden, denouncing Saudi Arabia's Middle East peace initiative and praising Palestinian suicide attacks, though it remains unclear whether the message is genuine.
2002-04-11: Al-Jazeera broadcasts previously unreleased video clips of Osama bin Laden and his deputy Ayman al-Zawahri, with plans to air the tapes in full on Thursday.
2002-04-15: Al-Jazeera broadcasts a videotape showing Osama bin Laden sitting with Ayman al-Zawahiri, who proclaims the September 11 attacks a "great victory," though it is unclear when the tape was made or whether the two are still alive.
2002-04-17: A Washington Post report says there is strong evidence Osama bin Laden was at Tora Bora in early December but escaped when the US relied on Afghan militias instead of large numbers of US ground troops, an account Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld dismisses as speculation.
2002-04-22: An Algerian man accused of being al-Qaida's European "gatekeeper" and of conspiring with Osama bin Laden to blow up Los Angeles airport appeared in a London court to fight extradition to the United States.
2002-05-01: US troops hunting fighters loyal to Osama bin Laden who fled into Pakistan came under rocket attack in Miram Shah, the first time US soldiers have been targeted inside the country.
2002-05-07: Canadian soldiers searching for Osama bin Laden’s body at Tora Bora took DNA samples from 23 buried al-Qaida fighters, but none appeared to be bin Laden.
2002-05-17: Mullah Omar is quoted in a newspaper interview as saying that Osama bin Laden is still alive.
2002-06-10: The Taliban's intelligence chief, Mullah Mohamed Khaksar, revealed that his 1999 offer to help the US depose Mullah Mohamed Omar was turned down, partly because the Clinton administration wanted to avoid interfering in Afghan politics, at a time when the Taliban had close ties to Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida.
2002-06-13: A Russian weekly newspaper reports that Mullah Mohammed Omar claimed in an email interview that Osama bin Laden is alive inside Afghanistan and threatened further terror attacks on the US.
2002-07-07: Al-Qaida spokesmen say Osama bin Laden's group is thriving and planning new attacks and assassinations, with bin Laden alive and well.
2002-07-15: A senior Arab journalist claims Osama bin Laden is still alive but was wounded in the shoulder during the US bombing campaign at Tora Bora, and that al-Qaida is planning further attacks in the US.
2002-09-11: Osama bin Laden went into hiding, traveling from Kandahar toward Kabul days after the September 11 attacks.

Osama bin Laden held several meetings with Pakistani nuclear scientist Sultan Bashiruddin Mahmood, starting in 2000 and continuing to July 2001, in which he asked how a nuclear bomb could be made and whether the scientist could help build one, according to the scientist's son.
2002-10-06: An audiotape broadcast on al-Jazeera, claiming to be a recording of Osama bin Laden, warned that the "youths of God" are planning more attacks against the United States.
An intercepted satellite phone call indicates Osama bin Laden is alive and meeting with Taliban leader Mullah Omar, according to Afghan intelligence.
2002-10-18: Saudi Arabia nominates former intelligence chief Prince Turki al-Faisal, who had several meetings with Osama bin Laden, as its next ambassador to London.
2002-11-23: A new 4,000-word letter attributed to Osama bin Laden is circulated among British Islamic extremists, calling for attacks on civilians, as the British Government warns al-Qaeda attacks on the UK are inevitable.
2002-11-28: Al-Qaida, the network of Osama bin Laden, is suspected of being behind an attack in Kenya targeting Israelis, though the article does not confirm responsibility.
2002-11-29: Swiss scientists at the Dalle Molle Institute for Perceptual Artificial Intelligence say they are 95% certain that a recent audio tape attributed to Osama bin Laden is a fake, conflicting with French research concluding it was probably genuine.
2003-01-19: A new document apparently signed by Osama bin Laden urges Muslims to stop fighting each other and unite against the "crusader coalition" attacking the Islamic world, with extracts published in the Saudi-owned newspaper Asharq al-Awsat.
2003-02-05: Tony Blair told Parliament there were “unquestionably” “links” between Osama bin Laden’s al-Qaeda group and Saddam Hussein.
2003-02-11: Al-Jazeera broadcasts a new audio tape attributed to Osama bin Laden, which the US had received an advance copy of five days earlier via the Qatari government.
2003-02-18: Saudi Arabia announces that at least 90 citizens will be prosecuted for links to Osama bin Laden's al-Qaida network.
2003-02-22: Terrorists linked to Osama bin Laden's al-Qaeda network are suspected of being behind the killing of British defence worker Richard Dent in Saudi Arabia.
2003-03-01: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, a senior al-Qaeda operative linked to Osama bin Laden, was seized in Rawalpindi, Pakistan.
2003-03-06: A Pakistani intelligence official claimed that captured al-Qaida leader Khalid Sheikh Mohammed told interrogators that Osama bin Laden is alive and living in the border region between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
2003-03-07: Reports claim two of Osama bin Laden's sons were caught after a shoot-out in southern Afghanistan, though US officials say there is no confirmation of the capture.
2003-03-12: The US says it has no information to substantiate reports that Osama bin Laden had been captured in Pakistan.
2003-04-27: Documents found in Baghdad by a British newspaper indicate that negotiations about a possible alliance between Saddam Hussein's regime and al-Qaeda took place in 1998, including discussions about a visit to Baghdad by Osama bin Laden.

A satellite phone purchased for Osama bin Laden’s representative and used by bin Laden and associates to plan the 1998 US embassy bombings in Tanzania and Kenya is reported to have been supplied through a purchase by a British-based Islamic dissident for whom MP George Galloway acted as secret emissary.
2003-05-12: Al-Qaida, led by Osama bin Laden, is suspected of carrying out the Riyadh bombings targeting Western and primarily American nationals.
2003-05-21: Al-Jazeera broadcasts a tape attributed to Ayman al-Zawahiri, an aide to Osama bin Laden, calling for attacks on Americans, Jews, and British interests.
2003-09-07: An audio tape purporting to be from Osama bin Laden's al-Qaida network threatens new attacks against Americans that would make them forget September 11.
2003-09-10: A videotape purportedly of Osama bin Laden was released on the eve of the second anniversary of the September 11 attacks, warning that the real battle with America and the West has not yet started.
Al-Jazeera broadcasts a 105-minute videotape showing Osama bin Laden with his deputy Ayman al-Zawahiri, who urges supporters to bury Americans in "the graveyard of Iraq."
The Bush administration agreed on a plan to oust the Taliban regime by force if it refused to hand over Osama bin Laden, according to a bipartisan commission report.
2003-10-19: Osama bin Laden released two audio tapes, videotaped threats, and filmed statements by suicide bombers, calling for renewed attacks on the West and on American and British troops in Iraq.
2004-01-04: An audiotape purporting to be from Osama bin Laden was aired on al-Jazeera, urging Muslims to rise up against American forces in Iraq and disparaging the US-backed Middle East peace "road map," with CIA analysts reviewing its authenticity.
2004-03-17: Al-Qaida, with Osama bin Laden's endorsement, declared its hope that George Bush would win the 2004 US presidential election.
2004-03-21: Article recounts 12 years of al-Qaeda attacks and plots involving Osama bin Laden, from the 1992 Aden hotel bombing through the 2004 Madrid train bombings.
2004-06-01: Prosecutors alleged that Osama bin Laden ordered defendants in the Istanbul bombings trial to attack an American airbase or Israeli cruise ship, but the trial was suspended when the court was deemed ineligible to hear the case.
2004-06-06: A senior Saudi diplomat claims the gunmen who attacked BBC journalists in Riyadh were linked to Osama bin Laden's al-Qaida network.
2004-06-16: The 9/11 commission reported finding no credible evidence of a collaborative relationship between Iraq and al-Qaida, noting that Osama bin Laden considered cooperating with Saddam Hussein but Iraq apparently never responded.
2004-10-05: Ten alleged al-Qaida members, including a man believed to be a senior lieutenant of Osama bin Laden, went on trial in France accused of plotting a bomb attack on Strasbourg's Christmas market.
2004-10-29: A new videotape of Osama bin Laden surfaced in which he admitted responsibility for the September 11, 2001 attacks for the first time and threatened new strikes against America.
2004-10-30: A videotape of Osama bin Laden was aired in which he addressed the US presidential election, prompting both candidates to reject his words and promise an unrelenting war against him.
2004-12-16: An audio tape purported to be of Osama bin Laden, referring to the attack on the US consulate in Jeddah, was posted on an Islamist website, with Colin Powell saying it appears to be bin Laden's voice.
2004-12-21: A former Jemaah Islamiyah operative testified in an Indonesian court that cleric Abu Bakar Ba'aysir met al-Qaida leader Osama bin Laden, an allegation Ba'aysir denied.
2005-02-24: The US funds television advertisements in Pakistan offering a $25m reward for information leading to Osama bin Laden, after a fruitless three-year manhunt.
2005-05-16: In a Spanish court, al-Jazeera war correspondent Tayssir Alouni described how he had interviewed Osama bin Laden weeks after the September 11 attacks.
2005-05-20: Pakistan's foreign minister claims Osama bin Laden is alive and on the run with a small band of fighters, while asserting that Pakistani forces have paralysed al-Qaida's communication network.
2005-07-09: Osama bin Laden's deputy Ayman al-Zawahiri sent a letter to Abu Musab al-Zarqawi setting out a four-step plan for al-Qaida to take control of Iraq after US troops leave, according to US intelligence officials.
2005-07-10: Article recounts over a decade of attacks attributed to Osama bin Laden and al-Qaeda, including the 7 July 2005 London bombings that killed at least 70.
2005-07-13: A Pew Centre survey finds that public confidence in Osama bin Laden has dipped sharply since May 2003 in Indonesia, Morocco, Lebanon and Turkey, with support for suicide bombings also declining across much of the Muslim world.
2005-08-04: In a video broadcast, Ayman al-Zawahiri, Osama bin Laden's deputy, warned of more destruction in London and said bin Laden had offered a truce conditional on withdrawing troops from Iraq.
2005-12-03: A leaked war log report claims that Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and Osama bin Laden’s financial adviser Dr Amin returned to Helmand after flying to North Korea and confirmed a deal for remote-controlled rockets for use against American and coalition aircraft.
2005-12-07: Al-Jazeera broadcasts as new an at-least-two-month-old al-Qaida video in which Ayman al-Zawahiri claims Osama bin Laden is still alive and leading the holy war, later saying the footage was aired by mistake.
2006-01-19: Osama bin Laden, in a taped dispatch, urged people to read William Blum's book Rogue States.

A tape recording purported to be of Osama bin Laden warns that preparations for a fresh wave of terror attacks on the US are under way and offers a truce if the US withdraws from Iraq and Afghanistan.
2006-02-05: Osama bin Laden's recommendation of William Blum's book Rogue State pushed it up 200,000 places on Amazon.com into the Top 25 list.
2006-03-01: President George W. Bush vowed to capture Osama bin Laden and Taliban leader Mullah Muhammad Omar during his first visit to Afghanistan since the US-led invasion.
2006-04-23: Osama bin Laden issued an audio tape calling on supporters to open a new front in Sudan and justifying attacks on civilians in the West.
2006-05-24: A purported Osama bin Laden tape was posted on an Islamist website denying that Zacarias Moussaoui played any role in the 9/11 attacks.
An audio tape purportedly from Osama bin Laden claims two imprisoned al-Jazeera journalists have no links to al-Qaida, though its authenticity has not been verified.
2006-06-30: An audio message purportedly by Osama bin Laden was broadcast eulogizing Abu Musab al-Zarqawi and warning the US, though it had not yet been verified by the CIA.
2006-09-07: Al-Qaida releases a videotape purporting to show some September 11 hijackers training in Afghanistan and meeting Osama bin Laden shortly before the 2001 attacks.
2006-09-10: Previously unseen footage of a smiling Osama bin Laden and other commanders apparently planning the September 11 attacks in a mountain camp was posted on the internet in a video purportedly from al-Qaida.
2006-09-11: Afghans in the eastern Afghan village where Osama bin Laden once lived mark the fifth anniversary of the September 11 attacks, recalling his time there and expressing mixed feelings about the war's aftermath.
2007-04-01: A former Cheshire parish councillor, Jane Felix-Browne, married Omar Osama bin Laden, a son of Osama bin Laden, in Islamic ceremonies in Egypt and Saudi Arabia.
2007-07-10: Osama bin Laden's deputy Ayman al-Zawahiri issued an audio tape warning Britain of a "very precise response" in retaliation for the knighthood given to Salman Rushdie.
Osama bin Laden's deputy, Ayman al-Zawahri, threatened Britain with retaliation over the knighthood awarded to Salman Rushdie in a video message.
2007-07-15: Omar bin Laden, son of Osama bin Laden, said he was "stunned and outraged" at publicity over his marriage to a 51-year-old British grandmother, confirming she is his second wife.
2007-09-06: A US-based monitor of jihadi websites reports that al-Qaida's media arm announced a forthcoming videotape of Osama bin Laden addressing the American people on the sixth anniversary of the September 11 attacks.
2007-09-07: Osama bin Laden released a video address, billed as a "message to the American people," in which he misquoted a Guardian documentary about a US soldier in Iraq.
2007-09-10: Al-Qaida's media arm announces that Osama bin Laden will release a video presenting the last testament of September 11 hijacker Abu Musab Waleed al-Shehri.
2007-09-11: Osama bin Laden is expected to release a video addressing the American people on the sixth anniversary of the September 11 attacks, according to an Islamist website announcement.
2007-10-21: Osama bin Laden released an audio tape urging insurgent groups in Iraq to unite and avoid divisions to defeat the US-led coalition.
2008-03-19: Osama bin Laden released an internet audio message threatening the EU over the publication of cartoons of the prophet Muhammad.
2008-05-16: An internet audio message purportedly from Osama bin Laden was released, marking the 60th anniversary of Israel's creation with a vow to continue fighting against Israel and its allies.
2008-07-21: Osama bin Laden's former driver, Salim Ahmed Hamdan, pleaded not guilty to terrorism-related offences at Guantánamo Bay, becoming the first detainee tried for war crimes.
2009-01-14: President-elect Obama argues that capturing or killing Osama bin Laden is not essential to protecting the US from al-Qaida-directed attacks.
An audio message purportedly from Osama bin Laden calls for Muslims to launch a holy war to stop the Israeli offensive in Gaza.
2009-03-14: In an audio recording broadcast on al-Jazeera, Osama bin Laden called Israel's offensive on Gaza a "holocaust" and accused some Arab leaders of collaborating with Israel, though the authenticity of the tape could not be verified.
2009-06-03: Osama bin Laden denounced Barack Obama in an audio recording, accusing him of sowing "revenge and hatred" in the Muslim world.
2009-07-23: A US report says Osama bin Laden's son Saad bin Laden was probably killed in a US drone strike in Pakistan's tribal areas earlier in 2009, though US intelligence officials cannot confirm his identity without a DNA test and are only "80 to 85%" certain he is dead.
2009-09-10: Anti-terrorism experts say Osama bin Laden's al-Qaida is under heavy pressure in Pakistan's tribal areas and struggling to attract recruits or carry out spectacular operations in Western countries.
2009-09-11: Al-Qaida released a video message marking the eighth anniversary of the September 11 attacks, in which Ayman al-Zawahri likened Barack Obama to George Bush, though Osama bin Laden did not appear in the video.
2009-09-14: An 11-minute audio recording attributed to Osama bin Laden was posted online by al-Qaida's media arm, in which he taunted Barack Obama as "powerless" to end the war in Afghanistan and criticized US backing for Israel.
2009-11-29: A Senate report finds that Donald Rumsfeld had the chance to kill or capture Osama bin Laden in December 2001 but let him escape from Tora Bora.
2010-12-16: According to a secret Guantánamo Bay intelligence report, Osama bin Laden escaped from Tora Bora in December 2001 with the help of a local warlord who provided fighters to guide him to safety in north-east Afghanistan.
2011-01-25: A former bodyguard for Osama bin Laden, Ahmed Ghailani, was sentenced to life in prison for his role in the 1998 US embassy bombings in East Africa.
2011-05-01: Barack Obama announces that Osama bin Laden has been killed in Pakistan.
Osama bin Laden was killed, prompting celebrations in Kenya among survivors of the 1998 embassy bombings but also fears of retaliation.
Osama bin Laden died in a US raid on his compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan.
Osama bin Laden, the al-Qaida leader behind the September 11 attacks, was killed by a US operation in Abbottabad, Pakistan, as announced by President Barack Obama.
2011-05-02: British Islamists warn that Osama bin Laden's death is "only the beginning," while radicals and mainstream Muslims offer mixed assessments of his legacy.
President Obama announces the death of Osama bin Laden.
Osama bin Laden was killed in a US special forces raid on a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan, where he had been living with three wives and several children for at least five years.
2011-05-03: Osama bin Laden's relatives maintained a discreet silence as more details emerged about his immediate family's involvement in the US raid in Abbottabad that led to his death.
2011-05-07: The Pentagon releases video footage of Osama bin Laden shot at his Abbottabad hideout, along with propaganda tapes seized during the US raid in which he was killed.
2011-05-09: President Obama says Osama bin Laden must have had a support network in Pakistan and calls on the Pakistani government to investigate possible complicity.
Pakistan's Prime Minister Yousaf Raza Gilani orders the army to investigate how Osama bin Laden managed to hide in the country for up to eight years.
2011-05-10: Osama bin Laden's adult sons attack the legitimacy of the US assault that killed their father and call for a UN inquiry into why he was not arrested and prosecuted.

In the wake of Osama bin Laden's death, his fifth wife Amal Ahmed al-Sadah and her daughter are being detained by Pakistani authorities, while a Yemeni al-Qaida supporter campaigns for their return to Yemen.
2011-05-12: The family of Osama bin Laden's youngest wife, Amal Ahmed al-Sadah, says she refused to leave her husband and wanted to be martyred alongside him; she is currently in Pakistani custody after being wounded in the raid that killed bin Laden.
2011-05-19: A tape recorded by Osama bin Laden before his death is released posthumously, in which he praises the Arab spring and predicts revolutions will spread across the Muslim world.
2011-06-15: Pakistani intelligence detains five alleged CIA informants who spied on Osama bin Laden before his killing in a special forces raid.
2012-02-09: The family of Osama bin Laden's youngest wife, Amal Ahmed al-Sadah, petitions Pakistan's chief justice to order her release and that of her children from Pakistani custody.
2012-02-22: Seventeen local health workers in Abbottabad were fired for their involvement in a CIA fake vaccination scheme intended to confirm Osama bin Laden's presence ahead of the May 2011 raid that killed him.
2012-04-26: Osama bin Laden's three widows and children were deported from Pakistan and were en route to Saudi Arabia.
2012-05-03: A memo released by the US military's Combating Terrorism Center shows Osama bin Laden sought advice on exploiting the tenth anniversary of 9/11 for propaganda, weighing US news channels before being killed four months before the anniversary.
2013-07-09: An official Pakistani commission report concludes that Osama bin Laden's decade-long stay in Pakistan was due to "collective incompetence and negligence" by intelligence agencies rather than a conspiracy, while not ruling out some plausibly deniable support.
